title: Relative flatness on an explicit affine base chart
statement: Let f:X→S be a scheme morphism, G a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] flat over f [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], and V an affine open of S. Put U=f⁻¹(V). The actual module H=(schemeOpenRestriction X U)(G) [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps] is flat over (f restricted to V) followed by the spectrum chart V≅Spec Γ(S,V). No quasi-compactness, separatedness or nonempty-open hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Lemma flat-module-characterize, Tag 01U4, final assertion; direct affine-section proof

proof.text: For an affine open V0 in V and U0 in f⁻¹(V) mapping into V0, take their images under the open inclusions. These images are affine and U1 lies in f⁻¹(V1) by image_morphismRestrict_preimage. Apply hflat to V1 and U1. morphismRestrict_appLE identifies the ring map; the section-module action agrees because the appIso of an open-subscheme inclusion is the identity. This proves flatness for ordinary restriction.

For postcomposition by the spectrum-chart isomorphism k, pull an affine open back along k. The map k.app is a ring isomorphism, hence flat by RingHom.Flat.of_bijective. The scalar tower and Module.Flat.trans transport the already obtained flatness. comp_appLE identifies the resulting action.

overFunctorEquiv identifies exact schemeOpenRestriction with ordinary restriction. Apply Scheme.Modules.IsFlatOver.of_iso to the inverse of this evaluated isomorphism, using flatness of ordinary restriction after postcomposition by the spectrum-chart isomorphism. This is the existing complete upstream proof; the mathematical node and both parent dependencies are retained.
